rule.statement: The amendment to the Finance Act No. 11 of 1963, which removed the protection for bona fide purchasers, does not prevent the Bank from acquiring the property.
rule.supporting_quote: The amendment brought to Section 71(2)(c)(ii) had been removed by the 1973 amendment to the said Act.

rule.statement: The Commercial High Court may refuse to permit a petitioner to lead oral evidence in proceedings under sections 224 and 225 of the Companies Act, if the matter can be determined on the basis of affidavits, documents, and written submissions.
rule.supporting_quote: The usual practice presently followed in the Commercial High Court is that the petitioner files a petition supported by affidavit together with supporting documents. The respondents thereafter file objections supported by affidavit together with supporting documents, and the matter is then fixed for inquiry and determined on the basis of such material and the written and oral submissions of counsel, without resort to viva voce evidence.

rule.statement: A person who is not (or no longer) of the Islamic faith cannot inherit from the estate of a deceased person of Islamic faith.
rule.supporting_quote: That must be taken as the law applicable to Safina’s estate.

rule.statement: A conclusion in [whether a conveyance is a forgery] must be arrived at only after considering the totality of the body of evidence in the case, in which, the expert opinion should be a striking item.
rule.supporting_quote: If the conveyance is a forgery, it must be concluded that it has not been executed in a lawful manner.
rule.statute_citation_verbatim: No evidentiary value can be attached to a conveyance which in its entirety or part thereof is a forgery, and thus must be rendered a nullity through judicial dictum.

rule.statement: A nomination of a successor to a holding under the Land Development Ordinance must be registered prior to the death of the owner for it to be valid.
rule.supporting_quote: Section 60 reads as follows; ‘60. No nomination or cancellation of the nomination of a successor shall be valid unless the document (other than a last will) effecting such nomination or cancellation is duly registered before the date of the death of the owner of the holding or the permit-holder.’
rule.statute_citation_verbatim: Section 60 of the Land Development Ordinance

rule.statement: A mandamus will not issue where it would be futile and could not be obeyed.
rule.supporting_quote: Thus, the primary reason attributed by the Court of Appeal in dismissing the Appellant’s application was that it became futile to issue a Writ of Mandamus under the circumstances.

rule.statement: A party cannot raise an issue of prescription for the first time in appeal if it is a mixed question of fact and law.
rule.supporting_quote: The underlying rationale to this principle is clearly set out by Jayawardena J, in Tilakaratne v Chandrasiri and another (supra) when his Lordship observed that;

rule.statement: The one-month time limit prescribed by Article 126(2) of the Constitution is a constitutional mandate and embodies the Latin maxim vigilantibus non dormientibus jura subveniunt (the law assists the vigilant, not the dormant).
rule.supporting_quote: The one-month time limit prescribed by Article 126(2) of the Constitution is a constitutional mandate and embodies the Latin maxim vigilantibus non dormientibus jura subveniunt (the law assists the vigilant, not the dormant).

rule.statement: A person who has entered into possession of land in one capacity is presumed to continue to possess it in the same capacity.
rule.supporting_quote: A person who has entered into possession of land in one capacity is presumed to continue to possess it in the same capacity- vide Corea Vs Iseris Appuhamy 15 N L R 65 and Tillekeratne Vs Bastian 21 N L R 12.

rule.statement: The institution of an action does not interrupt prescription, but only suspends it, and the defendant's possession remains uninterrupted if the plaintiff fails.
rule.supporting_quote: The argument of learned counsel for the plaintiff that Unambuwe v. Janohamy is wrongly decided cannot be accepted. The institution of an action ipso facto does not interrupt prescription but only suspends it. At the end, if the plaintiff succeeds, the defendant's possession is deemed to have been interrupted from the date of filing the action. If the plaintiff fails, the defendant's possession remains uninterrupted.

rule.statement: A co-owner has an interest in every part of the entire land, and can eject a trespasser from the whole land.
rule.supporting_quote: It is a commonsense principle that a co-owner has an interest in every part of the entire land. Thus, when a trespasser enjoys the fruits of the property the co-owner's rights are affected and he becomes entitled to eject the trespasser.

rule.statement: An appellate court should not interfere with the findings of facts of a learned judge who has had the advantage of seeing the demeanour of witnesses at the trial.
rule.supporting_quote: Further, an appellate court should not interfere with the findings of facts of a learned judge who has had the advantage of seeing the demeanour of witnesses at the trial. A similar view was expressed in the case of De Silva and others vs. Seneviratne and another (1981) 2 SLR page 7, where it was held;

rule.statement: A lessee who has entered into occupation is precluded from disputing his lessor's title until he has first restored the property in fulfilment of his contractual obligation.
rule.supporting_quote: Indeed, a lessee who has entered into occupation is precluded from disputing his lessor's title until he has first restored the property in fulfilment of his contractual obligation.

rule.statement: A person cannot transfer what they do not have.
rule.supporting_quote: He cannot transfer what he does not have.

rule.statement: Compound interest is not prohibited in Sri Lanka, and the respondent company is entitled to charge it in respect of the leasing facility.
rule.supporting_quote: On the basis of the above authorities and the reasoning therein, I am of the opinion that compound interest is not prohibited in Sri Lanka.

rule.statement: A notice of dishonour is not required for a promissory note when the drawer and drawee are the same person.
rule.supporting_quote: In applying those provisions the maker of a note shall be deemed to correspond with the acceptor of a bill, and the first indorser of a note shall be deemed to correspond with the drawer of an accepted bill payable to drawer’s order

rule.statement: A right to own property can only be denied by a process prescribed by law.
rule.supporting_quote: [A]mong the important rights which individuals traditionally have enjoyed is the right to own property. This right is recognised in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948). Article 17 (1) of which states that everyone has the right to own property and Article 17(2) guarantees that no one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his property.
rule.statute_citation_verbatim: Article 17 (1) of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)

rule.statement: The court should consider the admission made by the defendant when deciding the case, even if strict proof of the relationship is not required.
rule.supporting_quote: We observe that there is no specific mention in the judgement of the Provincial High Court of Civil Appeals that the learned Judge of the Provincial High Court of Civil Appeals had specifically treated this case as a rei vindicatio action when deciding this case. However, from the fact that the learned Judge of the Provincial High Court of Civil Appeals had required strict proof of the afore-said relationship, could be an indication that the learned Judges of the Provincial High Court of Civil Appeals may have been confused on this aspect of the case.

rule.statement: The Secretary must afford an opportunity to the Appellant to respond to the impugned letter if the Secretary were to act on it.
rule.supporting_quote: As Dr. Sunil Cooray points out [Principles of Administrative Law in Sri Lanka 4th Edition, page 477], “The traditional view was that the rules of natural justice applied only to decisions making process which the courts classified as ‘judicial’ and ‘quasi-judicial’. Today, that is not quite the idea”. Quoting Justice U de Z Gunawardena in Geeganage v. Director General of Customs [2001] 3 SLR 179, Dr. Cooray states; “that, the theory is obsolescent if not obsolete. Phrases that have come into use more recently in this context are the ‘duty of fair play’ ‘duty of fairness’ and ‘acting fairly’. Justice Mark Fernando remarked, in the case of Wijayapala Mendis v. Perera [1999] 2 SLR 110 at 148 “natural justice is fairness in action”.

rule.statement: A co-owner who claims prescriptive title must prove ouster or something equivalent to ouster, or place evidence sufficient to presume that ouster has taken place 10 years prior to filing the action.
rule.supporting_quote: Nothing short of ouster or something equivalent to ouster is needed to prove the commencement of an adverse possession against the other co-owners- Vide Corea V Appuhamy 15 NLR 65.

rule.statement: The winding up of a company is deemed to have commenced at the time of the presentation of the petition for winding up, and any disposition of the company's property made after this time is void unless the court otherwise orders.
rule.supporting_quote: Thus, the plain reading of the above section clearly shows that the date of commencement of the winding up of a company by Court must be taken as the date of filing of the application for winding up.
rule.statute_citation_verbatim: Section 262 of the Companies Act No. 17 of 1982

rule.statement: A novation discharges not only the original obligation but all obligations accessory to it.
rule.supporting_quote: A novation discharges not only the original obligation but all obligations accessory to it. Interest, penal charges, suretyships and pledges, accessory to the original contract, are thus all discharged

rule.statement: The question of identification of the land cannot be raised for the first time on appeal.
rule.supporting_quote: The question of identification of the land cannot be raised for the first time on appeal.

rule.statement: The Respondents have breached the rules of Natural Justice namely the rule Audi Alteram Partem when deciding to grant the permit to the 6th Respondent.
rule.supporting_quote: This has rendered the said decision and all subsequent actions relying on that decision null and void.

rule.statement: A plaintiff must establish both their title to the land and the devolution of title to the corpus in order to succeed in a partition action.
rule.supporting_quote: Considering the above, both the learned District Judge as well as the High Court of Civil Appeal was correct in holding that the Plaintiff had failed to establish, both, the title to the land sought to be partitioned as well as the devolution of title to the same.

rule.statement: A court exercising judicial functions has an inherent power to regulate its own procedure, save in so far as its procedure has been laid down by the enacted law.
rule.supporting_quote: A court exercising judicial functions has an inherent power to regulate its own procedure, save in so far as its procedure has been laid down by the enacted law, and it cannot adopt a practice or procedure contrary to or inconsistent with rules laid down by statute or adopted by ancient usage. - (Taken from Halsbury’s Laws of England 4th Edition Vol.10, Para 703.)

rule.statement: Mere execution of deeds does not confer title.
rule.supporting_quote: mere execution of deeds does not confer title.

rule.statement: Mere possession for a period of over ten years does not amount to possession discussed in Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.
rule.supporting_quote: Considering the above legal literature, I hold that mere possession for a period of over ten years does not amount to possession discussed in Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance; that a person claiming such possession is not entitled to succeed in a claim of prescription in terms of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance; and that in order to succeed in a claim of prescription, the claimant should prove that his possession is adverse, uninterrupted and undisturbed possession for a period of ten years.

rule.statement: A respondent to an appeal can invoke section 772 to challenge a finding in the decree in favour of another respondent only in exceptional circumstances.
rule.supporting_quote: It is necessary to now apply the aforesaid principles to the 9th defendant-respondent’s written objection under section 772 filed in the High Court and ascertain whether the 9th defendant-respondent had a right or entitlement to have his written objection considered by the High Court.

rule.statement: A person's right to hold property cannot be taken away without a specific provision of law.
rule.supporting_quote: The right of a person to hold property cannot be taken off without specific provision of law and there is no such law in operation.

rule.statement: A party cannot recall a witness to produce documents that were not listed in the initial stages of the trial due to negligence.
rule.supporting_quote: If these documents cannot be produced, no purpose would be served in recalling Wanigasekara the Notary Public. Further in my view Section 165 of the CPC cannot be utilized to cover up negligence of parties.

rule.statement: A person can possess property without occupying it, and to prove possession, it is not necessary to prove that he or she lives in the property or occupies it.
rule.supporting_quote: If a person does not occupy a property, does it mean that he does not possess the property? In my view, occupation and possession are two different things. One can possess a property without occupying the same.
rule.statute_citation_verbatim: Section 328 of the Civil Procedure Code

rule.statement: The court must consider the evidence led at the inquiry and not merely rely on the decision in Mowjood Vs. Pussadeniya.
rule.supporting_quote: The Court of Appeal Judgment has not considered the evidence led at the inquiry and merely arrives at a conclusion based on submission of counsel and the decision in Mowjood Vs. Pussadeniya.

rule.statement: A court of law has to consider the totality of evidence led and arrive at a conclusion, and slight acts of ingratitude are insufficient to revoke a deed of gift.
rule.supporting_quote: It is not correct to give your mind only to certain items of evidence. The material placed before court does not make it possible to interfere with the Court of Appeal Judgement. Therefore I affirm the Judgment of the Court of Appeal, and dismiss this appeal without costs.

rule.statement: A party cannot claim a document is not binding on them at a later stage, taking advantage of the fact that it was not duly attested, as they are estopped from doing so by law.
rule.supporting_quote: Either party who has signed a document cannot claim at a later stage, that the document is not binding on either party taking advantage of the fact that the document was not duly attested.
rule.statute_citation_verbatim: Sec. 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance

rule.statement: The court can infer a trust from attendant circumstances, even if a transfer is in the form of an outright sale.
rule.supporting_quote: Even though a transfer is in the form of an outright sale it is possible to lead parole evidence to show that facts exist from which it could be inferred that the real transaction was either.

rule.statement: Res judicata cannot be applied if the cause of action, thing, and person are not the same.
rule.supporting_quote: Firstly, in the present case the Plaintiff in 888/RE is different from the Plaintiff in 4677/L. The father and the son are two different persons. Res judicata cannot be applied.

rule.statement: A court in a partition action must satisfy itself as to the identity of the land sought to be partitioned, and for this purpose it is always open to him to call for further evidence in order to make a proper investigation.
rule.supporting_quote: In a partition action there is a duty cast on the Judge to satisfy himself as to the identity of the land sought to be partitioned, and for this purpose it is always open to him to call for further evidence (in a regular manner) in order to make a proper investigation.

rule.statement: A third party cannot plead the doctrine of laesioenormis, which applies only between vendors and vendees.
rule.supporting_quote: Laesioenormis is pleaded in cases only between the seller and the buyer with regard to the goods/property sold and bought. A third party outside the sale of the property cannot plead the doctrine of laesioenormis.

rule.statement: A defective proxy can be rectified and an opportunity should be given to the party to rectify the defects.
rule.supporting_quote: For the above reasons, I hold that defects in a proxy filed on behalf of a party in a case could be rectified and that an opportunity should be given to the party to rectify the defects.

rule.statement: The 1st Defendant was obliged to transfer the property to the Plaintiff-Appellant by way of transfer deeds as soon as the balance amount was paid.
rule.supporting_quote: According to clause 6 and 7 of the agreement to sell, the Plaintiff-Appellant need not wait till 31.12.1992 to make the balance payment; the 1st and 2nd Defendants are not empowered to wait till 31.12.1992 to write the deed of transfer upon payment of the balance amount; and no sooner the balance amount is paid the 1st and 2nd Defendants are obliged to transfer the property to the Plaintiff-Appellant by way of transfer deeds.

rule.statement: An Appellate Court will not interfere with findings of a trial Judge on question of fact.
rule.supporting_quote: An Appellate Court will not interfere with findings of a trial Judge on question of fact. Fradd V. Brown & Co. Ltd., 20 NLR 282.

rule.statement: A lessee's title is defaceable and dependent on the observance of the conditions and covenants in the lease agreement.
rule.supporting_quote: The position of a lessee does not differ from that of persons who are entitled to real rights. The title of a lessee is a defaceable one, and is dependent on the observance of the conditions an covenants incorporated in the lease agreement.

rule.statement: A partition decree cannot be the subject of any kind of private arrangement, between parties.
rule.supporting_quote: In the circumstances of this case it is observed that a partition decree cannot be the subject of any kind of private arrangement, between parties.

rule.statement: A Minister cannot order the issue of a Section 2 notice unless he has a public purpose in mind, and the purpose must be disclosed.
rule.supporting_quote: The minister cannot order the issue of a Section 2 notice unless he has a public purpose in mind. Is there any valid reason why he should withhold this from the owners who may be affected?

rule.statement: A party cannot make at trial a case materially different from that which they have placed on record.
rule.supporting_quote: Explanation 2 of S.150 of the Civil Procedure Code states the case enunciated must reasonably accord with the party’s pleading. And no party can be allowed to make at the trial a case materially different from that which he has placed on record, and which his opponent is prepared to meet.
rule.statute_citation_verbatim: S.150 of the Civil Procedure Code

rule.statement: The court rules that possession of land is presumed to have been delivered to the respondent based on a statutory presumption in favor of the execution of a writ of delivery of immovable property.
rule.supporting_quote: This Court rules on a statutory presumption in favour of the execution, in terms of Section 114 (d) of the Evidence Ordinance. This Section reads as follows;

rule.statement: The court has the discretion to grant relief under Section 759(2) of the Civil Procedure Code, even if the respondent has not been materially prejudiced.
rule.supporting_quote: The power of the Court to grant relief under S.759(2) of the Code is wide and discretionary and is subject to such terms as the Court may deem just. Relief may be granted even if no excuse for non-compliance is forthcoming. However, relief cannot be granted if the Court is of opinion that the respondent has been materially prejudiced which event the appeal has to be dismissed.

rule.statement: A partition decree should not be made unless the court is satisfied that the parties in whose favor it makes the decree are entitled to the property.
rule.supporting_quote: It is obvious that the Court ought not to make a (partition) decree, unless it is perfectly satisfied that the persons in whose favour it makes the decree are entitled to the property.

rule.statement: A marginal discrepancy in extent between two survey plans may be significant and not necessarily due to a computational error without expert evidence to that effect.
rule.supporting_quote: In such circumstances, even a seemingly minor discrepancy in extent may be significant.
